This is an unlisted page that is transcluded on [[Item Filtering]].

<onlyinclude>

===Formal Definition===

Formulas can be defined anywhere in the loot filter using <code>Formula[KEY]: FORMULA</code>. References to a formula must be in the form of <code>FORMULAKEY</code>. <code>Formula[_A]: STAT1!=STAT2</code> can be referenced by <code>FORMULA_A</code> or <code>%FORMULA_A%</code>.

Only '_' or 'A' to 'Z' may be used in a formula's key.

Aliases cannot be used in the definition.

===Inline Definition===

An inline formula definition is a formula inside a block <code>$f(STAT1!=STAT2)</code>. The 'f' must be lowercase and parentheses must match.

Aliases can be used in the definition.

===Item Input===

A formula can be used as a boolean, value or a part of an add condition.

{| class="wikitable"
! condition !! description
|-
| ItemDisplay[$f(STAT1+STAT2)>25] || value comparison
|-
| ItemDisplay[$f(STAT1+STAT2>20)] || boolean condition
|-
| ItemDisplay[$f(STAT1)+STAT2>15] || add condition
|}

The "truthiness" of a formula is based on a value being NOT equal to zero.
{| class="wikitable"
! formula !! description
|-
| 1.5 || true, since 1.5 != 0
|-
| TRUE || true, since TRUE (1) != 0
|-
| FALSE || false, since FALSE (0) == 0
|-
| 0 || false, since 0 == 0
|-
| .0000001 || true, x != 0
|}

===Item Output===

The result of a formula is a real number. It is rendered with either 0-2 decimal places depending on the fractional part with two decimal places. If a math error occurs or the value is too large to be rendered, the text is <code>f_err</code>. The maximum absolute value of a renderable result is 2^31 (2147483648).

{| class="wikitable"
! formula !! intermediate text !! rendered text
|-
| 1.49 || 1.49 || 1.49
|-
| 1.495 || 1.50 || 1.5
|-
| 1.494 || 1.49 || 1.49
|-
| 1.5 || 1.50 || 1.5
|-
| TRUE || 1.00 || 1
|-
| FALSE || 0.00 || 0
|-
| 0 || 0.00 || 0
|-
| .0000001 || 0.00 || 0
|}

===Operators===

<code>==</code>, <code>&gt;</code>, <code>&lt;</code>, <code>!=</code>, <code>&gt;=</code>, <code>&lt;=</code>, <code>+</code>, <code>-</code>, <code>*</code>, <code>&#47;</code>, <code>^</code>, <code>!</code>

===Variables===

All variables are case-insensitive. Each variable mirrors the code used in input or output.

====Parameterized====

Parameters are integers separated by a ','.

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! code !! example !! details || parameters
|-
| stat || stat3 || vitality || 1
|-
| multi || MULTI83,2 || Necromancer skills; must have two parameters || 2
|-
| charstat || CHARSTAT15 || gold in stash || 1
|}

===Functions===

All functions require one or more arguments (arity).

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! name !! details !! arity !! example
|-
| if || second arg if true, otherwise the third || 3 || IF(STAT3>100,TRUE,FALSE)
|-
| and || true if all values are true, false otherwise || 1+ || AND(STAT3>100,STAT0>100)
|-
| or || true if any values are true, false otherwise || 1+ || OR(STAT3>100,STAT0>100)
|-
| exp || Euler's number (e) raised to a power || 1 || exp(ln(STAT2))==STAT2
|-
| ln || logarithm of a number, base e || 1 || ln(STAT2)
|-
| floor || rounds a number down to the nearest integer || 1 || floor(1.5)==1
|-
| ceil || rounds a number up to the nearest integer || 1 || ceil(1.49)==2
|-
| round || rounds a number according to standard rules || 1 || round(1.49)==1; round(1.5)==2
|-
| min || minimum value || 1+ || MIN(STAT2,50)<=50
|-
| max || maximum value || 1+ || MAX(STAT2,50)>=50
|-
| mod || modulus of A/B || 2 || MOD(-17,5)==-2
|-
| average || average of n-args || 1+ || AVERAGE(8,8,8,8,8)==8
|-
| sqrt || square root of a non-negative number || 1 || SQRt(4)==2
|-
| pow || a number raised to a power || 2 || pow(2, 2)==4
|-
| count || number of true values || 1+ || COUNT(1,0,1,TRUE)==3
|-
| countif || number of values equal to the last value || 2+ || COUNTIF(1,0,1)==1
|-
| xor || true if an odd number of args are true || 1+ || XOR(1,0)==1
|-
| abs || absolute value of x || 1 || abs(-1)==1
|-
| sign || sign of x || 1 || sign(-1)==-1; sign(0)==0; sign(1)==1
|}

===Minor Details===

Tidbits that may or may not change.

* <code>AND</code> and <code>OR</code> are [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Short-circuit_evaluation short-circuited]
* constant expressions such as <code>POW(3,3)</code> or <code>IF(TRUE,STAT1,STAT2)</code> are evaluated once
* an input reference only requires the first letter (F) to be capitalized the rest is case-insensitive
* an output reference is always case-insensitive
